plan.chapter_thesis: Diffractive neural networks have transitioned from theoretical concepts to demonstrated applications across imaging, classification, and pattern recognition, yet their deployment maturity varies significantly between single-function tasks achieving near-electronic performance and complex multi-task systems remaining in the proof-of-concept stage.
plan.reader_takeaway: While ODNNs offer unique advantages in latency and energy efficiency for specific linear or single-function tasks, their widespread adoption is currently limited by a simulation-to-reality gap and environmental sensitivity that prevents them from consistently outperforming electronic baselines in general-purpose computing.

argument_sequence.purpose: Establish the foundational capability of ODNNs for standard image classification tasks as the primary benchmark for maturity.
Quantify the unique physical advantages of ODNNs regarding speed and energy efficiency compared to electronic counterparts.
Demonstrate advanced multiplexing techniques (polarization, OAM) that expand information capacity beyond simple intensity modulation.
Evaluate specialized imaging applications where ODNNs solve specific optical problems like super-resolution and achromaticity.
Assess the viability of hybrid optical-electronic systems and compressive sensing as pragmatic deployment strategies.
Analyze emerging reconfigurable hardware platforms (PCM, magneto-optical) aimed at overcoming static limitations.
Highlight multi-task learning capabilities enabled by multifunctional processors and metasurface co-design.
Identify critical barriers including environmental sensitivity, simulation gaps, and the current limitation to niche diagnostic tasks.

terminology_rows.note: All-optical machine learning framework using diffractive layers to perform inference at the speed of light.
Technique enabling multiple independent linear transformations within a single physical network by encoding data in polarization states.
Architecture combining passive diffractive optics for front-end feature extraction with electronic processing for non-linear activation and decision making.
Discrepancy between idealized training conditions and physical fabrication imperfections that degrades experimental performance.

explanation_block_rows.title: Benchmark Performance in Image Classification
explanation_block_rows.goal: Establish the baseline maturity of ODNNs by reviewing their success in standard datasets like MNIST and Fashion-MNIST.

explanation_block_rows.title: The Speed and Energy Advantage
explanation_block_rows.goal: Quantify the theoretical and measured gains in latency and power consumption that drive interest in ODNNs.

explanation_block_rows.title: Expanding Capacity via Multiplexing
explanation_block_rows.goal: Explain how polarization and orbital angular momentum are used to increase the computational density of diffractive systems.

explanation_block_rows.title: Specialized Imaging Applications
explanation_block_rows.goal: Detail applications where ODNNs excel at solving specific physical optics problems rather than generic classification.

explanation_block_rows.title: Hybrid and Compressive Architectures
explanation_block_rows.goal: Describe pragmatic approaches that combine optical preprocessing with electronic post-processing to mitigate optical limitations.

explanation_block_rows.title: Reconfigurable Hardware Frontiers
explanation_block_rows.goal: Review emerging materials and mechanisms that allow dynamic updating of diffractive weights post-fabrication.

explanation_block_rows.title: Multi-Task Learning Capabilities
explanation_block_rows.goal: Illustrate how single devices are being engineered to perform multiple distinct inference tasks simultaneously.

explanation_block_rows.title: Barriers to General Deployment
explanation_block_rows.goal: Synthesize the remaining challenges including environmental fragility and the gap between simulation and physical reality.

responsibility_coverage_rows.responsibility: Compare performance relative to electronic baselines
Identify unique strengths of optical inference
